centrality.caveat: Three manually annotated diagnostic cases are insufficient for a generalization claim.

evidence_localization.caveat: Measures target-file localization, not discrepancy classification.

blinded_locator.caveat: Synthetic/curated outputs; this does not imply 100% real-paper locator accuracy.

redbench.caveat: Twelve adversarial fixtures are a regression suite, not an estimate of production false-pass probability.

deepwalk.safety_behavior: abstained because no explicit output locator was proven and historical dependency sensitivity remained

perturbation_measurements.note: Independent adapter recomputes the central Pool A gap from raw released results without importing the authors' evaluation code.

conclusions: The strongest current components are safe abstention, claim/evidence provenance, paper ingestion, repository mapping, and synthetic blinded output localization.
The dominant real-paper bottleneck is workflow reconstruction: only 25% of eight diagnostic cases had confidently ordered workflows.
Environment detection is not the same as reproducibility: environment inference reached 100%, while only 25% were judged reproduction-ready.
Central-claim ranking improved qualitatively but remains weak at top-1 on the tiny annotated set (1/3).
Evidence localization is useful but incomplete: 50% recall@5 and 87.5% recall@10 on eight known discrepancy locations.
The isolated locator is substantially ahead of real-paper integration: 30/30 curated blinded cases versus 0/8 real diagnostic plans with a proven explicit locator.
No headline generalization claim should be made from SciCoQA diagnostic cases because the discrepancy labels are public.
